items.title: File Widerspruch against rejection of resident parking permit
items.quote: Möchten Sie die Entscheidung anfechten, erheben Sie Widerspruch – innerhalb eines Monats, gerechnet ab der Bekanntgabe, schriftlich, elektronisch mit qualifizierter Signatur oder zur Niederschrift bei der Stadt Beispielingen, Marktstraße 2, 70597 Beispielingen.
items.computation: Letter dated Wed 06.08.2025, sent by post. German administrative procedure law (§41 Abs. 2 LVwVfG BW, mirroring §41 Abs. 2 VwVfG) deems a letter sent by post delivered on the 3rd day after mailing (not the 4th day as the letter itself states – see warning). 06.08.2025 + 3 days = Sat 09.08.2025; this deemed-delivery ('Bekanntgabefiktion') day is not shifted for falling on a weekend, since it is a legal fiction, not an actual deadline day. The one-month Widerspruch period then runs per §31 VwVfG i.V.m. §§187 Abs. 1, 188 Abs. 2 BGB: the day of delivery (09.08.2025) is not counted itself; the period ends on the day of the following month bearing the same number, i.e. 09.09.2025 (Tuesday). 09.09.2025 is not a Saturday, Sunday or BW public holiday, so no further shift applies (§193 BGB not needed). If instead one applied the letter's own (legally incorrect) '4th day' rule, delivery would fall on Sun 10.08.2025, which under the standard weekend-extension of the delivery fiction moves to the next Werktag, Mon 11.08.2025, giving an end date of 11.09.2025. The earlier, legally correct date (09.09.2025) is used, per the rule to prefer the earliest plausible date when the letter's stated rule conflicts with actual law.

warnings: The letter states the deemed-delivery rule as 'am vierten Tag nach der Aufgabe zur Post' (4th day after posting), but the actual Baden-Württemberg administrative procedure law (§41 Abs. 2 LVwVfG BW) provides for delivery on the 3rd day after posting, not the 4th; using the letter's stated (incorrect) rule would push the Widerspruch deadline one to two days later (to 11.09.2025) — double-check this date, e.g. by confirming the actual date the letter was received, since a mis-stated rule that extends a deadline is a red flag worth verifying rather than relying on blindly.
No fee was charged for this decision ('Für diese Entscheidung werden keine Gebuhren erhoben'), so no payment is due despite the negative decision on the application.
